proposals.before: Loyalty and revolt shifted unpredictably. Han Yong's suppression of Teng Gorge, Wang Shouren's pacification of Tianzhou, the campaigns of Shen Xiyi and Yu Dayou, and the successes of Yin Zhengmao and Weng Wanda barely sufficed to bring the territory back under survey and control.
proposals.after: Loyalty and revolt shifted unpredictably. Han Yong's suppression of Teng Gorge, Wang Shouren's pacification of Tianzhou, the campaigns of Shen Xiyi and Yu Dayou, and the successes of Yin Zhengmao and Weng Wanda barely sufficed to restore order.
proposals.reason: 勘定 means to pacify and settle; “survey and control” imports an inapt sense of 勘 as land survey.

proposals.after: Early in the Xining era the local leader Luo Shinian submitted;

proposals.after: At the beginning of Xining in Song, the native man Luo Shinian came to surrender;

proposals.after: Under the Ming it was subordinate to Si'en Prefecture.

proposals.after: Under the Yuan it belonged to Zhen'an Circuit.

proposals.before: Yuan was subordinate to Tianzhou Circuit.
proposals.after: Under the Yuan it was subordinate to Tianzhou Circuit.
proposals.reason: The subject is Xiangwu Prefecture, not the Yuan dynasty.

proposals.after: Under the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.
proposals.reason: The subject is Dukang Prefecture, not the Yuan dynasty.

proposals.before: Yuan belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.
proposals.after: Under the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.
proposals.reason: The subject is Guohua Native Prefecture, not the Yuan dynasty.

proposals.before: In the first year of Hongwu in Ming, Huang Weijun was made native officer; for losing the seal it was abolished as a dong, demoted to native inspector.
proposals.after: In the first year of Hongwu in Ming, Huang Weijun was made native officer; because the seal was lost, the post was reduced to a dong and demoted to native inspector.
proposals.reason: 廢為峒 means the office was reduced to a dong, not that a dong was abolished.

proposals.before: Han belonged to Jiaozhi.
proposals.after: Under the Han it belonged to Jiaozhi.
proposals.reason: The subject is the Taiping region, not the Han dynasty belonging to Jiaozhi.

proposals.before: Taiping Prefecture lay northwest of Taiping fu.
proposals.after: Taiping zhou lay northwest of the prefectural seat.
proposals.reason: The Chinese locates 太平州 relative to 府 (the prefectural seat), not a second place also called Taiping Prefecture; the current rendering duplicates the toponym and collapses 州 and 府.

proposals.before: Early in the Ming the court promoted Zhao Ang to prefect.
proposals.after: Early in the Ming the court appointed Zhao Angsheng prefect.
proposals.reason: 以趙昂升為知州 is an appointment of 趙昂升; 升 belongs to the given name and does not mean promotion, and Zhao Ang omits 升.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Ming, Zhao Ang was promoted to prefect.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Ming, Zhao Angsheng was made prefect.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise drops 升 from 趙昂升 and renders 以…為 as promotion.

proposals.before: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi in Qing, he submitted, and Jizu was executed.
proposals.after: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi in Qing, submission was accepted, and Jizu was executed.
proposals.reason: The preceding sentence has already recorded Zhao Yinchang's murder, so a masculine pronoun 'he' wrongly makes the dead prefect the subject of 歸附.

proposals.before: Yuan belonged to Taiping Circuit.
proposals.after: Under the Yuan it belonged to Taiping Circuit.
proposals.reason: Literal English makes the Yuan dynasty the subject that belonged to Taiping Circuit; the Chinese 元屬太平路 means the prefecture belonged to Taiping Circuit in the Yuan.

proposals.before: Yuan belonged to Taiping Circuit.
proposals.after: Under the Yuan it belonged to Taiping Circuit.
proposals.reason: Same inverted subject as 元屬太平路: the place, not the Yuan, belonged to Taiping Circuit.

proposals.before: Yuan belonged to Siming Circuit.
proposals.after: Under the Yuan it belonged to Siming Circuit.
proposals.reason: Literal English makes Yuan the subject of 屬; the Chinese says the prefecture belonged to Siming Circuit in the Yuan.

proposals.before: Song was subordinate to Taiping Stockade.
proposals.after: Under the Song it was subordinate to Taiping Stockade.
proposals.reason: Literal English makes the Song dynasty itself subordinate to Taiping Stockade rather than the prefecture in the Song.

proposals.before: The Ming downgraded the fu to a prefecture and moved the seat to Bojiang Stockade.
proposals.after: The Ming downgraded the fu to a zhou and moved the seat to Bojiang Stockade.
proposals.reason: 降府為州 is a reduction from fu to zhou, not from fu to another fu/prefecture; the current rendering collapses the two ranks.

proposals.before: The succession reached Zhao Youjing, murdered by his younger half-brother Youtao.
proposals.after: The succession reached Zhao Youjing, murdered by his elder half-brother Youtao.
proposals.reason: 庶兄 means an elder brother born of a secondary consort, not a younger half-brother.

proposals.before: The line passed to Zhao Youjing, who was killed by his younger half-brother Youtao.
proposals.after: The line passed to Zhao Youjing, who was killed by his elder half-brother Youtao.
proposals.reason: 庶兄 is elder half-brother; younger reverses the relative-age term 兄.

proposals.before: Early in Hongwu Li Sheng submitted and the court set up Pingxiang Garrison.
proposals.after: Early in Hongwu, Li Sheng submitted and the court set up Pingxiang Garrison.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses the Hongwu reign label with the personal name Li Sheng; a comma is required after the reign.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Hongwu in Ming, Li Sheng submitted within and Pingxiang Garrison was established.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Hongwu in Ming, Li Sheng submitted and came over, and Pingxiang Garrison was established.
proposals.reason: Neifu is rendered as the calque submitted within, which obscures internal submission to the court.

proposals.before: Though it briefly fell under Annam, it returned to Ming control and was placed under Taiping Prefecture.
proposals.after: At that time it again belonged to Annam, yet it returned to Ming control and was placed under Taiping Prefecture.
proposals.reason: The Chinese says it again belonged to Annam; briefly is not in the source.

proposals.before: The Ming kept the arrangement; early in Hongwu Huang Weiqing was appointed prefect.
proposals.after: The Ming kept the arrangement; early in Hongwu, Huang Weiqing was appointed prefect.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses the Hongwu reign label with the personal name Huang Weiqing.

proposals.before: In Yongzheng 10 it was elevated to a regular prefecture.
proposals.after: In Yongzheng 10 it was changed to a regular prefect.
proposals.reason: The source names the circulating prefect office, matching the literal field; prefecture overstates the change.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Ming, it was abolished as a dong, with Xu Shangjue holding hereditary succession.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Ming, it was abolished and made a dong, with Xu Shangjue holding hereditary succession.
proposals.reason: The Chinese means reduced from a prefecture to a dong, not abolished as a dong.

decisions.reason: In this campaign sequence 勘定 means pacify and settle, not cadastral survey; “restore order” matches 仅得勘定 without importing land-survey 勘.
The given name is 世念; 念 is nian, so Luo Shinian is the correct romanization, not Shinan.
The literal line repeats the same inversion of 念 as nan; Luo Shinian restores the given name.
世知地州 uses 知 as the prefectural verb (知州), not “knowledge”; hereditary prefects of Di is the right sense.
English “appointed X Y” already names Wang Shouming to the Baishan native inspectorship; inserting “as” is only stylistic.

decisions.after: Ming changed it to Tianzhou Prefecture, then soon restored it as a zhou.
decisions.reason: 尋復為州 restores a zhou after the unit had been a fu; repeating “prefecture” erases the rank change. “Department (zhou)” is awkward beside this chapter’s usual rendering of 州.
元隸鎮安路 makes Guishun the subject in the Yuan period, not the Yuan dynasty itself subordinate to Zhen'an Circuit.
元屬田州路 means Sicheng belonged to Tianzhou Circuit in the Yuan, not that the Yuan belonged to the circuit.
明隸思恩府 likewise has Sicheng as subject under the Ming, not the Ming dynasty subordinate to Si'en.
元屬鎮安路 locates Xialei under Zhen'an Circuit in the Yuan; the dynasty is not the grammatical subject of 屬.
元隸田州路 refers to Xiangwu in the Yuan, not to the Yuan dynasty being subordinate to Tianzhou Circuit.
元屬田州路 has Dukang as subject in the Yuan; “Yuan belonged” inverts agent and place.
The same 元屬田州路 formula locates Guohua Native Prefecture, not the Yuan dynasty, under Tianzhou Circuit.
廢為峒 means the office was reduced to a dong after the seal was lost, not that a dong was abolished.
漢屬交阯 locates the Taiping region in Jiaozhi under the Han; the Han dynasty is not what “belonged to Jiaozhi.”
太平州，在府西北 places the zhou northwest of the prefectural seat (府), not northwest of another place called Taiping Prefecture.
以趙昂升為知州 appoints 趙昂升; 升 is part of the given name, not a promotion of a man named Zhao Ang.
The literal line likewise drops 升 from 趙昂升 and misreads 以…為 as promotion rather than appointment.
The preceding unit already records Zhao Yinchang’s murder, so “he submitted” wrongly makes the dead prefect the subject of 歸附.

元屬思明路 has Siling as subject in the Yuan; “Yuan belonged to Siming Circuit” inverts the geography.
宋隸太平寨 locates Siming under Taiping Stockade in the Song, not the Song dynasty itself as subordinate.
降府為州 is a rank reduction from fu to zhou; rendering both as “prefecture” collapses the change.
